name: George Ellis
bio: George Ellis (1753–1815) was an English satirist, antiquary and diplomat, editor of Specimens of the Early English Poets (1790) and a contributor to the Rolliad and the Anti-Jacobin.

The rondeau given here, mocking the salary of William Eden's commercial mission to Versailles, appeared in The European Magazine in December 1785; the Oxford Book of Eighteenth Century Verse attributes it to Ellis with a query.

poems.title: Rondeau, Humbly Inscribed to the Right Hon. William Eden
poems.author: George Ellis
poems.text:
Of Eden lost, in ancient days,
If we believe what Moses says,
A paltry pippin was the price,
One crab was bribe enough to entice
Frail human kind from Virtue's ways.

But now, when Pitt, the all-perfect, sways,
No such vain lures the tempter lays,
Too poor to be the purchase twice
Of Eden lost.

The Dev'l grown wiser, to the gaze
Six thousand pounds a year displays,
And finds success from the device;
Finds this fair fruit too well suffice
To pay the peace, and honest praise,
Of Eden lost.
